steps.title: Mark and image cranial window
steps.instruction: Make two small fiducial marks on the cranial window indicating anterior and medial directions. Record a fluorescence or bright‑field image of the vasculature (image A) and generate an in‑vivo retinotopic map (image B); the two images are naturally co‑registered because the optical axis is perpendicular to the window.

steps.title: Cardiac perfusion and capture image C
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the mouse with 5 % isoflurane and perform cardiac perfusion using the following fluids at the indicated flow rates: saline wash at 10 ml min⁻¹ for a total of 100 ml; DyLight 649‑lectin (5 µg ml⁻¹) at 5 ml min⁻¹ for 25 ml, then wait 5 min for lectin binding; 1 % PFA (see Recipes) at 5 ml min⁻¹ for 90 ml. While the brain remains in the skull, acquire a fluorescence image of the cranial window (filter 655/670 nm) – this is image C – confirming visibility of the fiducial marks.

steps.title: Dissect and flatten cortical sheet
steps.instruction: Collect the brain and keep it on ice. (Optional) Image the whole‑brain surface vasculature in bright‑field and fluorescence (filter 655/670 nm) for later registration (image D). In a Petri dish on ice, separate the two hemispheres with a razor blade, discard the non‑windowed hemisphere, cut off the olfactory bulb and all tissue posterior to the neocortex (cerebellum, posterior midbrain, hindbrain). Using a spatula, gently pull out thalamus, septum and striatum from the medial side and discard them. Flip the hippocampal formation out and separate it from cortex. Place the isolated cortical sheet on a gelatin‑coated slide with the pia surface against the glass, cover the opposite side with a piece of sponge, then place a second slide on top of the sponge. Insert two U.S. dimes (1.35 mm thickness) between the slides to set the spacing and clip both sides of the sandwich.

steps.title: Overnight fixation and sucrose infiltration
steps.instruction: Immerse the slide “sandwich” in 1 % PFA (see Recipes) overnight in a Petri dish at 4 °C. Remove the 1 % PFA, replace with 4 % PFA and incubate overnight. Then replace with 20 % sucrose (see Recipes) and incubate overnight. After the final incubation, remove the clips, cut the outer edge of the sheet into an asymmetric shape to expose anterior, posterior, medial and lateral sides, and acquire a fluorescence vasculature image of the flattened sheet (filter 655/670 nm) – this is image D.

steps.title: Tangential sectioning of flattened cortex
steps.instruction: Cool the microtome platform with dry ice for ~10 min and keep dry ice at both ends of the platform throughout sectioning. Embed the flattened cortex in OCT with the cortical surface facing up. Place a glass slide on top of the tissue and apply gentle finger pressure until the tissue freezes. Align the dissecting blade with the top surface of the glass slide, lock the platform, then warm the top slide with a finger to defrost and remove it, leaving the tissue surface parallel to the blade. Raise the platform until the frozen tissue contacts the blade; verify alignment by cutting test sections (~5 µm). Cut a first section of 150 µm thickness to ensure the whole cortical surface is captured, then continue cutting sections of 100 µm or 50 µm thickness through the entire cortex. Transfer each section to 1× PBS in a 24‑well plate.

steps.title: Cytochrome oxidase (CO) staining
steps.instruction: Wash each section in PBS (pH 7.4) three times for 5 min (~40 ml per wash). Mount sections on gelatin‑coated slides and let dry completely. Pre‑incubate with pre‑incubation solution (see Recipes) at room temperature for 10 min. Rinse 4 × 5 min with rinse solution. Incubate in incubation solution (see Recipes) for 1–6 h at 37–40 °C in the dark (or foil‑covered), checking the reaction every 0.5–1 h; stop when the tissue reaches the desired darkness. Rinse 3 × 3 min with rinse solution, then rinse once with de‑ionized water for 3 min.

steps.title: Dehydrate, clear, and DPX mount
steps.instruction: Perform all steps under a fume hood. Dehydrate sections through ethanol series: 50 %, 70 %, 90 % (3 min each). Wash twice in 100 % ethanol (3 min each). Wash once in xylene (5 min). Immediately place a coverslip with DPX mounting medium onto the xylene‑wet tissue (do not let xylene dry). Allow the DPX to solidify overnight.

steps.title: Capture bright‑field images
steps.instruction: Take bright‑field images of the DPX‑mounted sections (e.g., image series E showing layer 4 architecture of primary sensory and retrosplenial cortices).

substeps.instruction: 4 % (w/v) formaldehyde: dissolve 40 g paraformaldehyde in 800 ml PBS heated to ~60 °C (stirring, no boiling); raise pH to ~6.9 with 1 N NaOH dropwise, cool, filter, bring volume to 1 L with PBS, adjust pH to 6.9 with dilute HCl; store at 2–8 °C or aliquot and freeze.
1 % (w/v) formaldehyde: same as above but use 10 g paraformaldehyde; final volume 1 L; store as above.
0.2 M PB with 20 % sucrose (1 L): dissolve 4.8 g Na₂HPO₄ (anhydrous) and 22.72 g NaH₂PO₄ (anhydrous) and 200 g sucrose in distilled water, adjust pH to 7.4, bring to 1 L.
5 mg ml⁻¹ DAB stock (100 ml): dissolve 500 mg DAB, 0.788 g Tris‑HCl and 0.606 g Tris base in distilled water, adjust pH to 7.6, bring to 100 ml, aliquot 1 ml and freeze at –20 °C.

Pre‑incubation solution (0.05 M Tris‑HCl, 500 ml): dissolve 3.305 g Tris‑base and 0.485 g Tris‑HCl, add 137.5 mg CoCl₂ (final 275 mg L⁻¹) and 50 g sucrose (10 % w/v), adjust pH to 7.4, bring to 500 ml.

Incubation solution (25 ml): mix 20 ml 0.2 M PB with 20 % sucrose (pH 7.4), 4 ml DAB stock (final DAB 0.5 mg ml⁻¹), 3 mg cytochrome c (final 0.075 mg ml⁻¹), 0.008 ml catalase (final 64–640 U ml⁻¹), 0.1 ml DMSO (final 0.25 %), add distilled water to 25 ml (solution can be diluted to 40 ml if needed).
Rinse solution (200 ml): 0.1 M PB with 10 % sucrose, pH 7.4.
Additional 0.2 M PB with 20 % sucrose (100 ml) for optional use.
